name: Faded rosewood
lede: Faded rosewood is a greyed, dusty red-brown, the library's washed-out variant of [[rosewood]], and it reads as a muted brick rather than as wood.

sections.title: A modifier on an existing name
sections.body: The library builds this name in two steps: a base entry for [[rosewood]], then "faded" catalogued as its own separate variant [1]. The 1955 ISCC-NBS system files the same patch as grayish red, about 4.7 units away in CIEDE2000, and Ridgway's 1912 color atlas lists a matching block too, though our index carries no plate number for this particular one [1]. In Munsell notation it sits at 6.2R 4.4/3.1, a dark, low-chroma red; measured in LCH it has lightness 45, chroma 16 and hue 28 degrees, and [[charcoal]] than to a true rosewood brown, and in the same ISCC-NBS "grayish red" block as [[rose-brown]] [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our 23,781-painting archive, a match to this color appears in 165 paintings, 0.69 percent, as photographed; the within-painting lens finds it in 93 [2]. That puts it ahead of 58 percent of our named colors [2]. It peaks in the 1900s, 1.2 percent of the 1,674 paintings we have from that century, 20 paintings, about 2.4 times the archive's typical rate [2]. Inside a painting it most often plays a hidden color, in 52 percent of its appearances [2]. It is also over-represented in Indian paintings, 11 of 721, about 2.6 times what would be expected [2]. The earliest example in our data is from the year 1000; that is nine centuries before the name's earliest record in our sources, 1912, so the match is a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, never proof of the pigment or dye that early [2].
